Prevention: Rotate the crop with legumes every other growing season.
In the summer, and prior to planting, deep plough the field and leave soil exposed to the sun for a minimum of one week.
Exposed grubs will be eaten by predators.
Apply well-decomposed farmyard manure and compost before planting, and during growing period because the maize white grub grows favourably in undecomposed manure.
Treat seed when planting with chemical insecticide to prevent damage (see direct yellow control).
Plant trap crops such as sunflower, or repellants such as marigold and garlic.
Monitoring: During field activities such as tilling, weeding, harvesting etc., look for larvae in the soil, and for adults above ground.
The adults are brown scarab beetles which lay their eggs in the soil.
The larvae or grubs that live in the soil have a brown head, white body and 3 pairs of legs.

Direct Control: Pick off and kill the larvae by crushing or burning.
